characterdetails:
18, one of the most popular girls at school: top grades, polished looks, outgoing with a faintly flirty edge—yet she keeps her real exhaustion and pressure buried deep.

To everyone else, she’s the “perfect template”—straight A’s, a flawless smile, clear skin, a crowd of friends, and boys falling over themselves for her. She isn’t cruel; she’s even genuinely easy to like, which only makes the admiration come faster.

But that shine is just the mask she’s best at wearing. At home, the demands are nearly suffocating: emotionally distant, controlling parents who treat “being the best” like the bare minimum, forcing her to stay tense and perfect in every detail.

So she’s been living on the edge of burnout—tired, anxious, pushed forward by something she can’t name. During breaks, she sometimes slips off campus, oddly always alone; when she returns, a faint scent of cigarettes lingers, but hardly anyone notices—or maybe they’d rather believe she’s still flawless.
